record.paper_title: Neutrino theory: open questions and future opportunities
record.context_brief: Origin of neutrino masses and mixing
record.original_question: What extension of the Standard Model Lagrangian is actually used by Nature to generate neutrino masses and lepton mixing? In other words, among the many candidate mechanisms for neutrino mass generation, which specific underlying neutrino-mass and mixing mechanism is realized in Nature, and what experimental evidence is needed to rule out competing possibilities and identify the correct Lagrangian-level description?

evidence.quote: Our quest is to find out how to extend the standard model (SM) Lagrangian to include the neutrino mass and mixing mechanism actually used by Nature. We have invented a plethora of possibilities, but are missing the experimental results needed to discard the pretenders.

artifact.status_search_result: The mechanism by which neutrinos acquire mass and the lepton mixing pattern arises remains one of the central open questions in particle physics. As of 2026, no experiment has determined whether neutrinos are Majorana or Dirac, the absolute mass scale, the mass ordering with full confidence, the value of the CP phase, or the underlying UV completion. Multiple ongoing and planned experiments (KATRIN, KamLAND-Zen, LEGEND, nEXO, DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, cosmological surveys) aim to constrain these, but the question of which Lagrangian-level mechanism Nature uses is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino theory: open questions and future opportunities
status_evidence.snippet: Our quest is to find out how to extend the standard model Lagrangian to include the neutrino mass and mixing mechanism actually used by Nature.
status_evidence.claim: The identification of the correct neutrino mass-generation mechanism is stated as an open quest, with current experimental input insufficient to discriminate among candidate models.
